official.deadline_note: KOICA publishes the deadline as a month, not a single date: for the 2027 intake the application package was due to the applicant's KOICA country office or Korean Embassy in July 2026, and the specific deadline and procedures differ for each country office and embassy - applicants must verify with their own office. The published schedule then runs the university round (document screening, local medical check-up, interview) September-December 2026, admission notification November-December 2026, and arrival in Korea February 2027.
official.application_cycle: 2027 intake - 2027 KOICA Scholarship Program Application Guideline dated June 2026, entry February 2027
official.status_note: The 2027-intake KOICA Round closed in July 2026 (packages emailed to each KOICA country office or Korean Embassy); the published 2027 schedule places the cycle at the university round as of October 2026, and the next intake is announced by a pre-notice posted on the CIAT Notice board.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Tuition Fee: 'Full amount', paid by KOICA directly to the university (KOICA to University).
benefits: Monthly Allowance: KRW 1,200,000 per month (KOICA to University to Participant)
Tuition Fee: Full amount, paid by KOICA directly to the university
Air Fare: economy class flight ticket, based on actual expense, at the time of initial entry and final departure
Settlement Allowance: KRW 600,000 (Master) / KRW 1,200,000 (Doctoral), once; Scholarship Completion Grants: KRW 300,000 (Master) / KRW 600,000 (Doctoral), once, before departure

Accommodation in a university dormitory (condition varies depending on universities), National Health Insurance at actual expense (approx. KRW 81,000 per month) and Private Medical Insurance for unexpected accidents or illnesses

Extracurricular activities: part of the expenses for study visits, workshops, Korean language classes and others, plus pre-departure orientations, arrival briefings and settling-in support including immigration procedures and transport to the institution
eligibility: Citizenship of a designated country: all applicants must be citizens of countries KOICA selects from the OECD DAC List of ODA Recipients - 96 designated countries for 2027 (Africa 41, Central and South America 18, Asia 14, Pacific 12, Middle East/CIS/Eastern Europe 11), subject to annual change
Government official status with an official nomination from the applicant's own government for the KOICA Scholarship Program

(Preferably) under the age of 40, and in good health both mentally and physically for the full duration of the program (applicants with severe illness are not eligible; applicants with disabilities but in good health are eligible)

Master's applicants: bachelor's degree (as of July 31, 2026) with preferably 2 years of experience in the field of study; Doctoral applicants: master's degree (as of July 31, 2026) with preferably 3 years of experience after completing the master's degree program

Strong command of English in both speaking and writing; an official English proficiency test score is not required at the KOICA Round but may be required by certain universities at the University Round

Prior Korean government degree scholarship holders are not eligible (bachelor's degree scholarship holders may apply for the master's course), previously cancelled KOICA scholars are not eligible, applicants who completed a KOICA or other Korean government-funded master's cannot apply for the KOICA master's, and doctoral applicants must have no experience of receiving foreign assistance for doctoral degree scholarship programs
requirements: Applicants must meet the criteria set by the university they apply to and submit all required documents listed in the Program Information provided by that university, and must read the application guidelines and Program Information in their entirety
Applicants must apply to only one program among the listed courses (2027: 15 courses - 11 master's and 4 doctoral - across eight Korean universities)
Preferably employed by their government during and after the program, engaging in the specialized area of their study as an official servant of their government

University-level criteria can add course-specific rules, e.g. Yonsei admits non-Korean applicants with non-Korean parents, applicants who completed formal education from elementary to higher education outside Korea, holders of an accredited master's degree, or those with equivalent academic qualifications
Passing the KOICA country office / Korean Embassy interview does not guarantee final acceptance; university document screening, medical check-up and interview follow
documents: KOICA Application Forms Part 1-4: Part 1 Applicant Information, Part 2 Terms & Conditions, Part 3 Medical History Questionnaire, Part 4 Nomination
Letter of recommendation from the applicant's government (office in charge of ODA or the abroad scholarship program), bearing the institution's official seal - no specific format is mandated
Scanned copy of a valid passport (English name must match the passport exactly; valid until at least 6 months after the expected date of return) - never send the original passport
Completed 'Document Checklist' for the admission package, submitted by email to the KOICA country office and Korean Embassy

University Round documents (only for those who pass the KOICA Round): the university application form plus everything listed in the Program Information - e.g. authenticated graduation certificates and transcripts, English test score or evidence of English proficiency, curriculum vitae, and copies of the applicant's and parents' passports (Yonsei example)

Original university application documents sent by international courier to the submission point set for each course; submitted documents are non-returnable, and applicants who submit false documents cause their institution to be restricted from recommending new applicants for three years
selection_criteria: KOICA Round: document screening of the emailed application package (submitted documents are non-returnable) and an on-site interview at the KOICA country office or Korean Embassy, with a phone interview possible where no office is present in the applicant's country or the applicant lives far from the capital

University Round document screening reviews the application package comprehensively, including the reputation of the applicant's undergraduate school, undergraduate GPA including the grading scale, English proficiency, current affiliation and work experience
Local medical check-up at the applicant's own expense after document screening, then a final medical check-up in Korea after arrival - only applicants who pass it become KOICA SP Fellows
University interview, plus a mandatory written/essay test at some universities; failing to follow university instructions may result in withdrawal from the process

KOICA HQ collects the interview results from each university and finalizes the successful applicants, who then submit original documents, obtain a D-2 study visa and required vaccinations, and enter Korea in February for the 2027 intake
coverage: Tuition: full amount, paid by KOICA directly to the university
Living costs: monthly allowance of KRW 1,200,000 plus university dormitory accommodation

Travel: economy class flight ticket at initial entry and final departure, based on actual expense (participants pay any additional airfare if they change the itinerary, and expenses caused by the participant's own fault are not covered)
Insurance: National Health Insurance at actual expense (approx. KRW 81,000 per month) and Private Medical Insurance for unexpected accidents or illnesses
Extra support: settlement allowance, scholarship completion grant before departure, and part of extracurricular activity expenses (study visits, workshops, Korean language classes)
application_method: Prepare all required documents for the admission package, complete the Document Checklist, and email the KOICA application package to the relevant KOICA country office and Korean Embassy by the submission date set by that office

Participate in the on-site interview conducted by the KOICA country office or Korean Embassy (a phone interview may be arranged after consulting the office where none is present in the country or the applicant lives far from the capital)
Those who pass the KOICA Round apply to the university through its official online admission system or by email as instructed in the university's individual guidance
Take the local medical check-up and attend the university interview (and essay test where required) between September and December 2026 for the 2027 intake

After final acceptance, send original documents by international courier to the submission point set for the course, then prepare the D-2 study visa and any additional vaccinations directed by the university
Enter Korea in February 2027, complete KOICA orientation and the medical check-up in Korea, then begin the degree program
official.application_route: Two rounds: email the KOICA application package to your KOICA country office or Korean Embassy (KOICA Round), then apply to the university through its own admission system (University Round); general inquiries koica.sp@koworks.org
official.study_mode: Full-time, on-campus degree program in Korea (KOICA-funded stay of 17 months for the master's and 36 months for the doctoral program)
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must be citizens of one of the 96 designated countries on KOICA's 2027 list (Africa 41; Central and South America 18; Asia 14; Pacific 12; Middle East, CIS and Eastern Europe 11), selected from the OECD DAC List of ODA Recipients and subject to annual changes
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the program is designed for government officials from KOICA's partner (developing) countries; applicants must be citizens of a designated country and be officially nominated by their own government
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Government officials nominated by their own government who apply to only one listed course; each course's Program Information sets field-specific criteria, e.g. Yonsei's master's programs restrict admission to non-Korean applicants or those who completed their formal education outside Korea or hold an accredited master's degree
official.research_requirement: KOICA's CIAT site publishes a dedicated 'SP Thesis' section, and each Program Information sets the thesis and degree requirements - for example, fellows in Yonsei's master's programs are strongly recommended to complete their thesis within the 17-month stay
official.duration: Master's Degree Program: 17 months; Doctoral Degree Program: 36 months (the detailed program duration for each university is specified in its Program Information)
official.description: KOICA presents the Scholarship Program as 'a prestigious initiative designed to empower aspiring leaders from KOICA's partner countries', offering post-graduate opportunities at both master's and doctoral levels since 1997 and 'specially designed for government officials'. The 2027 cycle under the CIAT fellowship programme offers 15 courses (11 master's and 4 doctoral) at eight Korean universities for entry in February 2027.
official.region: KOICA partner countries - 96 designated countries for 2027 across Africa, Central and South America, Asia, the Pacific and the Middle East/CIS/Eastern Europe; study takes place in Korea
official.program_type: Korean government-funded international postgraduate scholarship administered by the Korea International Cooperation Agency (KOICA) under the CIAT fellowship programme
official.english_requirement: KOICA requires 'a strong command of English, both in speaking and writing' and states that an official English proficiency test score is not required at the KOICA Round, though certain universities require evidence at the University Round - the Yonsei Program Information requires a minimum of TOEFL iBT 68, TOEFL ITP 520, IELTS 6.0, TEPS 259 or TOEIC 650 (scores valid five years), waived for nationals of English-official countries with three years of English-medium education, those who completed a degree in an English-primary country, or on a minister/governor letter

not_confirmed: deadline_central - KOICA publishes only the application month (July 2026 for the 2027 intake) and states the specific deadline is set by each KOICA country office and Korean Embassy
catalogue_url - no official catalogue page is published
verification.notes: Amounts, benefits, schedule, documents and eligibility were verified against KOICA's own 2027 Scholarship Program Application Guideline (June 2026) attached to official CIAT Notice post 390552, plus the CIAT Scholarship Program Info, Application Procedure and 2027 Program Information files on koica.go.kr; the application date itself is set locally by each country office/embassy.

applicant_utility.summary: This is a full-ride Korean government scholarship for serving government officials: KOICA pays full tuition, pays KRW 1,200,000 every month, houses you in a university dormitory and flies you to Korea and back, plus insurance and completion grants. Entry is gated by a two-round process that starts with an official nomination from your own government, submitted by email to your country's KOICA office or Korean Embassy. Applications for the 2027 intake closed in July 2026 and that cycle is now at university screening, so the useful action today is to contact that office and get apostilles, English scores and a nomination lined up for the next pre-notice. Budget your own money up front: KOICA explicitly does not reimburse anything spent on the selection process.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A serving government official, preferably under 40, from a KOICA-designated partner country, whose ministry can issue a sealed official nomination letter.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your country is on KOICA's designated list for the cycle and identify your KOICA country office or Korean Embassy contact before the round opens, since deadlines and submission mailboxes differ by office.
Request the official government recommendation letter from the office in charge of ODA or abroad scholarships early, and make sure it carries the institution's official seal.
Obtain an apostille or consular confirmation on your degree certificate and transcripts now - you will need them again for the visa and alien registration card.
Check that the English name on your passport matches every application form exactly and that the passport stays valid at least six months beyond your expected return.
Sit an accepted English test (TOEFL iBT/ITP, IELTS, TEPS or TOEIC) or assemble an exemption file such as a degree completed in English, because university rounds like Yonsei demand written evidence.
Set aside cash for the unreimbursed selection costs: document authentication, the local medical check-up, international courier and the D-2 visa fee.
common_rejection_risks: Applying without the official government nomination, or with a recommendation letter that lacks the institution's seal.
A passport English name that does not match the application forms - KOICA warns this delays visa processing and can unravel late-stage admissions.
Missing apostilles or consular confirmation on degree documents, or originals that fail document checks, which leaves final candidates on hold or disqualified.
Going quiet on university instructions during the second round - the guideline states that failing to follow the university's instructions may result in withdrawal from the process.
Being ruled ineligible for holding a previous Korean government degree scholarship or a cancelled KOICA scholarship, or for applying to the master's after completing a government-funded master's.

Treating the embassy interview as a formality: passing it does not guarantee acceptance, and the university re-screens undergraduate school reputation, GPA with grading scale, English and work experience.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Visa fees, local transportation, stopover expenses and the entire selection process - document authentication/apostille, the local medical check-up, express mail and any university application fee - are not covered; personal spending such as laundry, phone and mini-bar-style charges also comes out of the monthly allowance.
document_audit: KOICA Round documents go by email only, and procedures differ for each country office and embassy, so confirm the exact mailbox, deadline and checklist with your own office instead of relying on the central page.
Never post your original passport - a scan is what KOICA wants, and it must remain valid six months past your expected return.
KOICA forms must be typed in English with your original handwritten signature (not cursive) and need no apostille, while certificates and transcripts do.
Originals go by international courier to the submission point set for your specific course, and submitted documents are non-returnable - keep certified copies of everything.
False documents are punished by a three-year ban on your institution recommending any new applicants, so the reputational cost lands on your ministry, not just you.
Each university's Program Information carries its own document list and deadline; read it in full because responsibility for inaccuracies rests with the applicant.
alerts: KOICA sets no single deadline - each KOICA country office and Korean Embassy sets its own within the published month, so a generic 'July' window can hide a much earlier local cut-off.
You may apply to only one program in the cycle, so choose deliberately before the window opens.

The 2027-intake round is already closed (July 2026) and that cycle is at university screening with admission notifications in November-December 2026, so any page still advertising the 2027 round as open is out of date; watch the CIAT Notice board for the next pre-notice.
Acceptance is only final after the medical check-up in Korea, so keep health documentation consistent between the local exam and the Korean one.
Deferral of entry, leave of absence and schedule adjustments for personal circumstances are not permitted once you are admitted, and voluntary withdrawal is irreversible.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Email the KOICA package to your country office or embassy, clear the on-site interview, then follow the university's own online admission system for the second round and courier originals only after final acceptance.
